To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are more often placed in special schools than in regular schools, and that this placement pattern has been relatively stable in the past 20 years.

(1) the use of a comprehensive, multidisciplinary assessment procedure is recommended for children who are considered for placement in an assessment unit; (2) the results of the assessment procedure should be interpreted by a multidisciplinary team; and (3) the assessment procedure should include a thorough evaluation of the child's basic school skills, social adequacy and physical appearance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of predicting suitability for special education of children in an Assessment Unit, and the variables that are used in the prediction.
the identification of factors which influence the decision of the educational placement of children in an Assessment Unit and their subsequent placement in special education.
the problem of ascertainment of children who are in need of special education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variables used to ascertain the children were not sufficiently comprehensive and that the criteria used for placement were not sufficiently precise.

the assessment of children should include an assessment of their basic school skills, their intellectual abilities, their social adequacy, the recommendations of the teachers and parents, their physical appearance, their behaviour, and the recommendations of the psychologist.
the variables which are most highly related to educational suitability are the following: intellectual ability, basic school skills, and the recommendations of the school and the assessment team.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important variables in deciding placement of children in assessment units are the child's intellectual ability, his basic school skills, his social adequacy, the placement recommendations, and the physical appearance of the child.
the assessment unit is a valuable resource for special educators.
a combination of factors are important for the decision to place a child in a special school.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most successful way for children to achieve their educational goals is to have an individualized educational program (IEP).
we have shown that the use of the principal component analysis method is a good way to identify factors that influence the placement of children in an educational assessment unit.
the use of a machine learning approach for predicting educational suitability of children in an Assessment Unit is feasible.
